title: Fiber: one unit of work per component

slides.say: Fiber is React’s reconciliation engine since React sixteen. Its headline feature is incremental rendering.

slides.text: A fiber = a JS object for one component: its type, key, props, and links to child, sibling and parent.
slides.say: A fiber is a plain JavaScript object with information about one component: its type, its key, its props, and pointers to its child, sibling, and parent fibers.

slides.text: Think of it as a "virtual stack frame" React can pause, resume, reuse or abort.
slides.say: Think of it as a virtual stack frame. Because React manages these frames itself, it can pause work, come back later, reuse it, or throw it away.

slides.text: Up to two fibers per component: current (on screen) and work-in-progress. (Simplified.)
slides.say: Each component has at most two fibers: the current one on screen, and a work in progress one. This is a simplified view of internals that may change.
